# package capture

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-modbus-capture/capture"
```

Package capture holds the model of a Modbus capture: what a device answered, and when. It defines the types every encoding stores (Header, Target, Stream, Sample, End), the streaming Reader and Writer interfaces the encodings implement, and the invariants a capture satisfies (Checker).

The package does no I/O. Values are raw request and response PDUs; nothing is decoded.

## Constants

```go
const (
	VersionMajor = 0
	VersionMinor = 1
)
```

Format version written by this library. Readers accept files with the same major version and any minor version. Major version 0 marks the draft format (see docs/FORMAT.md): files written now are not readable once the format is frozen as 1.0.

```go
const (
	// TagProvenance records the tools and operations that produced a capture.
	TagProvenance = "provenance"
	// TagSource records the original file names of a merged capture.
	TagSource = "source"
)
```

Reserved tag keys.

```go
const (
	RolePoll     = "poll"
	RoleScan     = "scan"
	RoleIdentity = "identity"
	RoleSnapshot = "snapshot"
	RoleOther    = "other"

```

Conventional stream roles.

```go
const (
	// MaxStringLen is the longest string (label, producer, host, tag key or
	// value) in bytes.
	MaxStringLen = 64 << 10
	// MaxTags is the largest number of tags on a header or target, and
	// MaxTagBytes the largest total size of their keys and values.
	MaxTags     = 256
	MaxTagBytes = 1 << 20
	// MaxTargets and MaxStreams bound the definitions of a capture.
	MaxTargets = 1 << 16
	MaxStreams = 1 << 16
	// MaxRequests bounds the number of distinct (stream, request) pairs whose
	// last response a change-only capture tracks.
	MaxRequests = 1 << 20
	// MaxTickNS is the largest tick size: 1 s.
	MaxTickNS = uint64(time.Second)
)
```

Limits that keep readers bounded on hostile input. Writers enforce them too, so that every capture written can be read back.

```go
const DefaultTickNS = 1000
```

DefaultTickNS is the default tick size: 1 µs.

```go
const MaxPDULen = 253
```

MaxPDULen is the largest Modbus PDU: 253 bytes (function code and data).

## Variables

```go
var ErrCorrupt = errors.New("capture: corrupt")
```

ErrCorrupt is wrapped by the error a reader returns for input that is not a valid encoding, or whose records break the model's invariants.

```go
var ErrTruncated = errors.New("capture: truncated")
```

ErrTruncated is wrapped by the error a reader returns when the input ends before the capture does: in the middle of a record or block, or (binary) without an index. Records returned before it are valid. A capture read that far has no recorded end.

### func Copy

```go
func Copy(dst Writer, src Reader) error
```

Copy writes every record of src to dst and closes dst with the end of src (End{} when src has none). It stops at the first error and does not close dst then.

### func Diff

```go
func Diff(a, b *Capture) string
```

Diff describes the first difference between a and b, or returns "" when they are equal (see Equal).

### func Equal

```go
func Equal(a, b *Capture) bool
```

Equal reports whether a and b hold the same capture: the same header, the same definitions in the same order, the same samples in the same order with byte-identical PDUs, and the same end. Empty and nil maps are equal.

### func IsReadFunction

```go
func IsReadFunction(fc uint8) bool
```

IsReadFunction reports whether fc is a read function of the Modbus specification: FC01 to 04, 07, 08, 11, 12, 17, 20, 24 and 43. Vendor, user-defined and other function codes are not supported.

### func IsWriteFunction

```go
func IsWriteFunction(fc uint8) bool
```

IsWriteFunction reports whether fc changes the device (FC05, 06, 15, 16, 22 and 23). Captures never hold such samples.

### func ParseVersion

```go
func ParseVersion(s string) (major, minor int, err error)
```

ParseVersion parses a text version "major.minor" and checks that this library reads it: the major version must be VersionMajor.

### func Write

```go
func Write(w Writer, rec Record) error
```

Write writes one record to w. An End is not written: it is passed to Close.

## Types

### type AddressValues

```go
type AddressValues struct {
	Function uint8
	Start    uint16
	Values   []uint16
}
```

AddressValues are the raw values of an FC01–04 sample, one per address: coils and discrete inputs as 0 or 1, registers as unsigned 16-bit words. Nothing is decoded beyond that.

#### func SplitAddresses

```go
func SplitAddresses(s *Sample) (AddressValues, bool)
```

SplitAddresses splits the response of an FC01, 02, 03 or 04 sample into one value per requested address. It returns false for other functions, for exception responses, and for a response whose size does not match the request. Coil and discrete-input bits come least significant bit first: the LSB of the first data byte is the first requested address.

### type Checker

```go
type Checker struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Checker checks a stream of records against the model's invariants, in the order they are written or read:

  - the header: a tick of 1 ns to 1 s, a wall-clock start between 1970 and 2262 (Unix nanoseconds in a uint64 and an int64), bounded strings and tags;
  - every string (labels, producer, host, tags): valid UTF-8 without a carriage return, so that every text encoding keeps it;
  - targets: positive unique ids, a known transport and parity;
  - streams: positive unique ids, a target defined before;
  - samples: a stream defined before; request and response PDUs of 1 to 253 bytes; a request of a read function of the specification (see IsReadFunction), FC08 with a data-returning sub-function only and FC43 with MEI type 14 only; a response with the request's function code or its exception code; an exception response only when the header records exceptions; in a change-only capture, no response equal to the previous response to the same request of the same stream;
  - the end: not before any sample.

Sample times need not increase: samples of concurrent streams may be written slightly out of order.

#### func NewChecker

```go
func NewChecker(h Header) (*Checker, error)
```

NewChecker checks h and returns a Checker for the records that follow it.

#### func (Checker) Admit

```go
func (c *Checker) Admit(s Sample) (bool, error)
```

Admit checks a sample to be written. It returns false, without error, for a sample the capture does not store: an exception response when the header does not record exceptions, or an unchanged response in a change-only capture.

#### func (Checker) End

```go
func (c *Checker) End(e End) error
```

End checks the capture end. No record may follow it.


MaxAt returns the latest sample time checked so far.

### type End

```go
type End struct {
	Known bool

```

End is the capture end. A capture whose end was not recorded (for example one truncated by a crash) has Known false.

### type Header

```go
type Header struct {
	// TickNS is the size of a tick in nanoseconds (1 to 1e9; default 1000).
	TickNS uint64
	// WallStart is the wall-clock time at tick 0, at nanosecond resolution.
	// It is stored in UTC.
	WallStart time.Time
	// ChangeOnly marks a change-only capture: a sample whose response equals
	// the previous response to the same request of the same stream is not
	// stored.
	ChangeOnly bool
	// Exceptions marks a capture that records exception responses. Without
	// it a capture holds none.
	Exceptions bool
	// Producer names the tool that wrote the capture.
	Producer string
	// Tags are free key/value pairs. Reserved keys: TagProvenance, TagSource.
	Tags map[string]string
}
```

Header describes a capture as a whole.

#### func (Header) Duration

```go
func (h Header) Duration(t Ticks) time.Duration
```

Duration returns t as a duration since the capture start. It saturates at the largest duration.

#### func (Header) Ticks

```go
func (h Header) Ticks(d time.Duration) Ticks
```

Ticks returns d in ticks, rounded down. A negative d is 0.

#### func (Header) Time

```go
func (h Header) Time(t Ticks) time.Time
```

Time returns the wall-clock time of t.

### type Reader

```go
type Reader interface {
	// Header returns the capture header.
	Header() Header
	// Next returns the next record. After the last one it returns io.EOF.
	Next() (Record, error)
}
```

A Reader returns the records of a capture in order. Definitions come before the samples that use them; the End, when the capture has one, comes last.

### type Writer

```go
type Writer interface {
	WriteTarget(t Target) error
	WriteStream(s Stream) error
	WriteSample(s Sample) error
	// Close completes the capture with its end and flushes it. It does not
	// close the underlying io.Writer. Use End{} when the end is unknown.
	Close(end End) error
}
```

A Writer writes a capture. Definitions must be written before the samples that use them. Writers check every record (see Checker) and return an error for an invalid one. A sample that a change-only capture does not store, or an exception response in a capture without Exceptions, is dropped without error.
